items.title: Nonmonotonic Magnetic Correlations in Decorated Lieb-Lattice Anderson Models
items.summary: The interplay between electronic correlations and lattice geometry can strongly modify the competition between magnetic correlations and local singlet formation in multiorbital Hamiltonians. Here we use determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations to investigate two periodic Anderson-like models constructed by selectively hybridizing localized orbitals to the inequivalent sites of a Lieb lattice. The resulting geometries possess partially filled flat bands and different sublattice imbalances. We examine the evolution of local spin correlations and orbital-resolved magnetic structure factors as the hybridization is increased. Although correlations between hybridized orbitals evolve relatively smoothly toward local singlet formation, the longer-range magnetic correlations exhibit a striking nonmonotonic dependence on hybridization. In particular, we observe a pronounced suppression at intermediate hybridization followed by a substantial recovery on undecorated lattice sites. We discuss these results in relation to earlier studies of depleted periodic Anderson models and the constraints imposed by Lieb's theorem. Our findings illustrate how selective hybridization and flat-band structure can produce unusual redistributions of magnetic correlations in strongly interacting multiorbital systems.

items.title: Normal-state exponential muon-spin relaxation and its implications for time-reversal symmetry breaking in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$
items.summary: The low-temperature increase of the zero-field muon-spin relaxation rate in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ has long been regarded as evidence for spontaneous internal fields associated with time-reversal-symmetry-breaking (TRSB) superconductivity. Here we directly test this interpretation using muon-spin rotation/relaxation ($μ$SR) measurements on high-quality Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ single crystals. For all four samples, the onset temperature of the additional exponential relaxation in the zero-field$μ$SR data, $T_Λ$, lies below the bulk superconducting transition temperature $T_{\rm c}$, even in the absence of applied strain. More importantly, in transverse-field $μ$SR measurements we find a quantitatively similar exponential relaxation in a field of 80 mT applied along the crystallographic $c$ axis. This field exceeds the upper critical field of the crystals studied in transverse-field geometry and suppresses bulk superconductivity, demonstrating that the characteristic relaxation persists in the normal state. Measurements below the upper critical field reveal an additional superconducting mixed-state contribution superposed on this normal-state channel. Our results show that the zero-field $μ$SR relaxation in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ cannot, by itself, be regarded as a unique signature of superconducting TRSB. They call for a reassessment of a key experimental signature of TRSB in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ and highlight the need to distinguish superconducting and normal-state relaxation channels in other unconventional superconductors.

items.title: Tailoring Phonon Transport in Bi-based Quaternary Half-Heusler alloys for Thermoelectric Applications
items.summary: Quaternary half-Heuslers (QHHs) are substitutionally disordered derivatives of conventional halfHeusler (HH) compounds, which offer a potential route to modify phonon transport and enhance thermoelectric performance. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric properties of the quaternary half-Heuslers ZrHfRh2Bi2, ZrHfIr2Bi2, Zr2RhIrBi2, and Hf2RhIrBi2 using first-principles calculations and anharmonic lattice dynamics. Among four compounds, ZrHfRh2Bi2 and Zr2RhIrBi2 exhibit semiconducting electronic structure and others are semimetallic in nature. Both the semiconducting compounds show favorable electronic transport properties. However, quaternary substitution substantially modifies the phonon dispersion, lowering the average phonon group velocity by about 17-22% relative to the parent compounds while leaving the anharmonic scattering rates comparable. The combination of high power factor and low kl results in high thermoelectric performance, with maximum ZT values of 2.28 and 2.18 at 1000 K for p-type ZrHfRh2Bi2 and Zr2RhIrBi2, respectively, with maximum thermoelectric power conversion efficiency 16.3% for p-type ZrHfRh2Bi2. Further reducing the grain size enhances the thermoelectric performance, with maximum ZT values of 2.51 and 2.58 at 1000 K for p-type ZrHfRh2Bi2 and Zr2RhIrBi2, respectively, at a grain size of 30 nm. Our results demonstrate that combining substitutional disorder with grain boundary engineering, provides an effective strategy to enhance the thermoelectric performance of HH compounds.

items.title: Revealing the growth of structural length in glass-forming liquids without using dynamical information
items.summary: Dynamical heterogeneity underlies the dramatic slowdown of supercooled liquids and has long been a central topic in glass physics. Despite considerable progress in identifying structural motifs and order parameters correlated with dynamical heterogeneity, a general characterization of structural descriptors remains elusive because they can vary among glass formers and are not generally known \emph{a priori}. To address this challenge, we establish a unified framework that can be applied to varieties of glass formers to extract structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity directly from their static configurations. The framework combines a graph neural network (GNN) with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Across three canonical three-dimensional glass-forming models, the resulting structural field exhibits a characteristic correlation length that tracks the corresponding dynamical correlation length. Notably, a network trained on small systems can be applied to larger systems without retraining, indicating that the extracted features are encoded in local and mesoscopic structural correlations. These results demonstrate that static configurations encode structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity and establish a scalable, interpretable route for extracting them.

items.title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe2-xTex Polytypic Heterostructures
items.summary: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure-superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2-xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range-from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T' structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8)shows suppressed Tc (~ 2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin-orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.

items.title: Predictive Renormalization-Group Theory of Universality Classes in Nonlinear Systems
items.summary: Universal scaling behavior appears across a wide range of nonlinear systems despite substantial differences in their governing equations and physical mechanisms. We develop a renormalization-group (RG) framework that identifies two complementary RG mechanisms underlying such universality. First, scale invariance generates RG fixed points corresponding to asymptotic self-similar solutions. Second, repeated RG transformations eliminate non-scale-invariant irrelevant structures, causing broad classes of equations to flow toward the same fixed points and thereby form universality classes. The framework applies to finite-time singularities, long-time intermediate asymptotics, stochastic Edwards--Wilkinson growth, nonlinear diffusion, density-dependent biological diffusion, and fluid-interface dynamics. In each case, it reproduces known scaling behavior and identifies the associated universality class through explicit irrelevance criteria. A central feature of the framework is its predictive character. Once a scale-invariant fixed point is identified, the theory predicts whole classes of nonlinear equations sharing the same asymptotic self-similar solution. While the diffusion class is partially supported by existing mathematically rigorous results, most universality classes identified here have not previously been established and therefore constitute testable predictions. These results provide a unified RG perspective on universality in nonlinear systems and show that universality emerges from the same fundamental RG principles that underlie critical phenomena.

items.title: Local moment magnon spectrum in conduction electron tunnelling
items.summary: The surface tunnelling spectrum of a dual system consisting of localised moments with antiferromagnetic order coupled to conduction electrons by on-site exchange interaction is investigated. In the static approximation of the local moment order it is known that magnetic band reconstruction leads to an anomalous tunnelling spectrum at the magnetic ordering vector of local moments although the latter cannot contribute directly. In this work we consider dynamic effects by including the scattering of conduction electrons from the local moment magnon excitations. They lead to self energies and renormalisation of conduction states which in turn appreciably modify the tunnelling spectrum beyond the influence of static order, interpreted as the appearance of magnon sidebands.

items.title: Impact of capacity volatility and input substitutability on supply chain resilience
items.summary: Supply chains are inherently vulnerable to stochastic shocks due to their sequential dependence on production. Employing the Feld-Barthelemy (FB) framework [Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 134} 217401 (2025)], we investigate how capacity volatility and input substitutability determine critical demand that a supply network can withstand. By controlling the variance in production capacity, we show that reducing capacity volatility is more effective than increasing average capacity in long supply chains, highlighting the necessity of firm-level stabilization. In the extended FB model that incorporates substitute suppliers, we find that diversifying suppliers independently increases critical demand, even when average production capacity remains constant. Surprisingly, improving network connectivity can also increase critical demand without changing the number of suppliers. This implies that the effect of input substitutability on critical demand is heavily influenced by network topology, even in the absence of stock. Our findings reveal that mitigating capacity volatility and securing structural diversity in supply routes are just as crucial to supply chain resilience as expanding stock capacity.

items.title: Recoverable Necking Enabled by Reverse Phase-Boundary Motion in Liquid Crystal Elastomers
items.summary: Strain localization is often associated with plastic flow and permanent deformation. Here we show that a tensile neck in a crosslinked nematic network can undergo nearly complete recovery through reverse phase-boundary motion, leaving little residual deformation. In a monodomain liquid crystal elastomer stretched perpendicular to its initial director, this recovery occurs during an isothermal loading-unloading cycle. Digital image correlation resolves the process as the retreat of interfaces separating low- and high-stretch regions, where the high-stretch domain shrinks while previously necked material thickens, despite substantial mechanical hysteresis. Within the recoverable-necking regime, increasing temperature lowers the loading plateau stress but raises the unloading plateau stress. A nonconvex constitutive description provides an energetic basis for the coexistence of the two stretch states, while gradient regularization accounts for the finite width of their interfaces through an equilibrium reference profile. These results identify the spatial mechanism of neck recovery and distinguish recoverable strain localization from mechanical reversibility in an orientationally ordered polymer network.

items.title: Electrostatic and Quantum Transport Engineering of Multilayer Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions for Improved TER and RA Trade off
items.summary: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for non-volatile memory and neuromorphic computing, but achieving a high tunnel electroresistance ratio (TER) with a low resistance-area (RA) product remains challenging. In this work, TiN/Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ (HZO)-based FTJs containing zero to three TiO$_2$ and IGZO-based quantum wells (QWs) are analyzed using the Miller ferroelectric (FE) polarization model integrated with the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism to examine the effects of QW material and thickness on polarization and transport. TiO$_2$-based structures exhibit higher polarization and TER than IGZO-based structures. At a read bias of 0.1 V, the uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structure, with 1-nm-thick QW and insulating layer (IL) layers, gives a TER of $2.71\times10^{10}\%$ and an RA product of $5\times10^4~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$, compared with $5.95\times10^7\%$ and $2\times10^5~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$, respectively, for IGZO. Both uniform and non-uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structures exhibit resonant tunneling (RT) and negative differential resistance (NDR) associated with QW-confined states. Increasing the first QW thickness to 1.38 nm, while keeping the second QW and both IL layers at 1 nm, shifts the confined-state energies and modifies resonant transport. The selected non-uniform structure achieves a TER of $2.95\times10^{11}\%$ and an RA product of $1.25\times10^3~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$ at a read bias of 0.1 V. Elastic scattering changes the amplitude and width of QW resonant-transmission peaks, with a stronger effect on the low resistance state (LRS) than on the high resistance state (HRS). These results show that QW material and thickness optimization can improve the TER--RA trade-off, while electrode screening and elastic scattering further influence polarization-dependent transport in multilayer FTJs.

items.title: Generating grain boundary structures at a specified energy with a symmetry-constrained diffusion model
items.summary: Grain boundaries (GBs) govern many properties of polycrystalline materials, and inverse design would make the GB structure itself a design variable. Crystal generative models such as MatterGen operate on periodic cells, which contain two GBs. The cell energy defines a single GB only when the two are equivalent, but existing models do not enforce this equivalence. Building on MatterGen, we developed a symmetry-constrained diffusion model in which the two GBs are related by a symmetry operation: atoms near one GB are generated, and those near the other are reconstructed through a symmetry projection applied at every denoising step. We applied it to the $Σ5(210)[001]$ symmetric tilt GB in Al, conditioning generation on the GB energy from a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). All 350 generated structures kept a geometrically equivalent GB pair after relaxation. Given a target GB energy, the model generated structures at that energy: for the three in-range targets with many nearby training structures, 44% to 70% fell within $\pm 0.1$ J/m$^2$ of the target. Tracking weakened at higher energies and failed outside the training range. Of the 91 near-target structures, 90 matched no training structure under the adopted geometric criterion, indicating that the model can propose configurations near the target energy that are distinct from the training structures, a capability that could help identify unknown metastable GB structures observed in experiments. Building GB-pair equivalence into generation thus makes GB properties well-defined design targets, enabling inverse design of GB structures.

items.title: Agentic programs: an emerging form of scientific software in computational materials science
items.summary: Computational materials science has traditionally delegated algorithmic tasks to computers while leaving scientific judgments to humans. In this Perspective, we argue that agent harnesses built on large language models (LLMs) enable an emerging form of scientific software, agentic programs, integrating deterministic algorithms with bounded LLM-based judgment, task-specific verification, episodic maturation, and complete delegation. We illustrate these characteristics through DeMARS, which constructs atomistic models from experimentally measured disordered crystal structures.

items.title: Quantum effects on the Peierls stress for screw dislocations in α-Fe
items.summary: The large discrepancy between the Peierls stress calculated using atomistic methods and that measured in experimental studies is well known. Despite significant research efforts over the past decades, our understanding of this mismatch remains limited. This work presents a multiscale study on the kinetics of screw dislocations in α-Fe at 0.7K, employing the phonon description of temperature and using the Concurrent Atomistic-continuum (CAC) method as the simulation tool. Our simulations are shown to preserve the Bose-Einstein distribution of phonon modes and reproduce the nucleation and propagation of kink pairs. Large-scale CAC simulations with dislocation line lengths ranging from 0.1 to 2.1 microns, a typical range of lengths for screw dislocation lines, are performed, providing a quantitative and mechanistic understanding of the phonon-dislocation in α-Fe. The experimentally measured Peierls stress in α-Fe has been successfully reproduced, and the quantum effects on Peierls stress are quantified. Dependencies of phonon-dislocation interactions on dislocation line length and specimen size are explored and discussed.

items.title: Ultraslow vorticity modes in colloidal fluids
items.summary: In the conventional unsteady-Stokes picture, vorticity generated by a transient disturbance relaxes rapidly through viscous diffusion once the forcing ceases. This view presumes a quiescent solvent. In colloidal and biological fluids, thermal motion continually perturbs the surrounding fluid, raising a natural question: can equilibrium fluctuations, mediated by hydrodynamic coupling, sustain vorticity over mesoscopic scales and times? Here, using high-speed confocal microscopy of moderately dense colloidal suspensions, we reconstruct the conditional mean hydrodynamic response to Brownian displacements of prescribed magnitude and direction. We find a long-lived, spatially structured vorticity field that decays far more slowly than predicted by unforced unsteady-Stokes dynamics. A coarse-grained phenomenological model based on fractional Brownian motion, constrained by independently measured single-particle subdiffusion, quantitatively captures its temporal and spatial decay. These findings reveal a field-level manifestation of hydrodynamic memory in fluctuating low-Reynolds-number flows, with implications for transport and collective dynamics in complex fluids.

items.title: Kinetic Arrest of a Disordered First-Order Phase Transition in Strained V2O3 Thin Films
items.summary: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) in epitaxial V2O3 thin films as a prototype. By defining a coarse-grained mesoscopic order parameter representing the metallic volume fraction coupled to the primary structural monoclinic distortion, we formulate a Time-Dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) framework integrated with a non-local elastic interaction kernel and an Imry-Wortis quenched disorder landscape. We derive an explicit dynamic criterion for the kinetic arrest boundary TK(E) by analyzing the divergence of the intrinsic order-parameter relaxation time relative to experimental observation timescales. Our framework rigorously decouples the thermodynamic driving force from the kinetic activation barrier. We demonstrate that epitaxial substrate-induced clamping elevates local elastic barriers, pinning domain boundaries and stabilizing an arrested, inhomogeneous mosaic of metallic and insulating phases down to cryogenic temperatures. The simulated transformation kinetics exhibit an Avrami exponent suppression to values n < 1, reflecting slow, hindered domain-wall propagation. Furthermore, we examine the effect of an external electric field as an isothermal mechanism that lowers this kinetic barrier, providing a phenomenological description of threshold de-arrest and multi-level resistance states. We critically discuss this electronic barrier-lowering mechanism in comparison with electrothermal Joule heating, establish diagnostic criteria to distinguish them, and contextualize these non-equilibrium dynamics with related phenomena in disordered superconducting films.

items.title: Power Law Transients in Perovskite Photoluminescence
items.summary: Carrier dynamics and recombination in perovskite thin films are often explored through transient photoluminescence (PL) measurements and subsequent analysis based on single/multi-exponentials. In contrast, here we show that several experimental PL transients reported in literature vary as power laws with time and are not multi-exponentials. Puzzlingly, the existing theoretical methods are ill-equipped to explain the origin and implications of such power law trends. Our analysis resolves this puzzle and correlates the power law exponents with the trap distributions. Curiously, we show that PL transients could vary as $t^{-2}$ even in the presence of dominant monomolecular recombination while the existing theory associates this unique trend exclusively with dominant bimolecular recombination. These findings identify the limits of applicability of concepts such as differential lifetime and highlight the need for predictive modeling synergistic with insightful data analysis towards performance optimization of perovskite optoelectronic devices.

items.title: Shear thinning confines the wall forcing: laminar chaotic mixing of Carreau fluids in a rotating arc-wall mixer
items.summary: With two-dimensional simulations of Carreau fluids of power-law index $N$ from 1 to 0.4, I study how shear thinning modifies laminar chaotic mixing in an open channel stirred by three arc-shaped wall segments rotating back and forth periodically, the upper one in anti-phase with the two lower ones. The outlet mixing efficiency falls monotonically, by 14 percent from $N=1$ to 0.4, mostly between $N=0.85$ and 0.6. The bulk flow and its chaotic saddle are nearly unaffected. Shear thinning acts instead through a thin layer of reduced viscosity around the moving arcs: the geometric penetration length of the wall forcing shortens as the 0.3 power of the time-mean wall viscosity, within 4 percent over a fourfold range of forcing. This confinement weakens the stretching, and the penetration length predicts the mixing efficiency ($r^2=0.97$). The optimal Strouhal number stays close to 0.7 for all fluids, but shear thinning narrows the range of efficient periods. A lamellar model indicates that the relative penalty of shear thinning grows with the Peclet number. As the injected power scales with the wall viscosity, the mixing efficiency per unit energy rises 2.6-fold from $N=1$ to 0.4, and at equal energy per unit volume, with a faster rotation, the fluid with $N=0.4$ mixes as well as the Newtonian one, and better at larger energies. In wall-driven mixers, the reach of the forcing, not the bulk viscosity, is the quantity to control.

items.title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: a quantum Monte Carlo study
items.summary: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal $d$-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background $π$-flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and $d$-wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the $d$-wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.

items.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
items.summary: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system also navigates the charge-stability landscape to stabilize the quantum dot around optimal operating points. These results demonstrate a ``compute-in-place'' platform, with a logic and power footprint suited to future cryo-CMOS integration, that provides autonomous stabilization of quantum dots at desired operating points, creating an auto-tuning system for spin qubits that is resilient to electrostatic drifts, changing noise profiles, and two-level fluctuations.

items.title: Probing Plasmonic Oscillations in 2D Moir'e Nanocrystal Superlattices by Low-Loss EELS
items.summary: Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) has been established as a powerful analytical technique for investigating the oxidation state, band structure, and dielectric properties of materials with exceptional spatial resolution. Inspired by twisted 2D materials, we utilize low-loss EELS to examine the plasmonic excitations in 2D moiré Au nanocrystal superlattices (NCSLs) formed by liquid-air interface self-assembly using a double-dipping method. This approach produces stacked hexagonal layers that can be twisted, forming moiré patterns in NCSLs whose twist angles are precisely measured via scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Low-loss EELS effectively mitigates challenges arising from fabrication-induced non-uniformity and reveals a blue shift in plasmonic excitation when comparing single-layer, double-layer, and twisted configurations. This sharply contrasts with the optical spectroscopy measurements, which show an overall red shift relative to the EELS data. The high spatial resolution of STEM-EELS further demonstrates that twist-induced symmetry breaking strongly influences plasmonic behavior. Coupled dipole modeling explains the observed discrepancies: the electron beam excites out-of-plane polarization modes unavailable to optical probes, while optical measurements average over ensembles. Our findings highlight that EELS provides complementary information to optical spectroscopy for understanding how structural arrangements at the nanoscale influence collective electronic properties, advancing the design of plasmonic metamaterials.

items.title: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction
items.summary: Most existing equivariant architectures for Hamiltonian prediction propagate features in direct-sum spaces of irreducible spherical tensors, whereas the target Hamiltonian is naturally an operator block in a direct-product representation over local orbital and spin bases. This representation mismatch fragments contiguous Hamiltonian blocks, obscures direct manipulation of orbital couplings, and organizes features into irregular angular-momentum components that require numerous transformations and are poorly aligned with efficient hardware execution and memory management. To address both the representation mismatch and computational bottleneck, we propose DP-Learner, an equivariant learning framework that performs message passing directly on Hamiltonian-like operator blocks in the direct-product space. Theoretically, we propose Lie-generator-based directional embedding and invariantly weighted left--right products and contractions that preserve equivariance to SO(3), SU(2), and spatial inversions, without explicit Clebsch--Gordan decomposition or inverse reconstruction. Methodologically, we instantiate this principle as a Transformer architecture, in which Hamiltonian-like feature matrices or tensors evolve through equivariant operators in the direct-product space, while non-linear invariant scalar routing controls structured gating over matrix units, directional propagation, attention, and environment-embedded context interactions. We further construct MP-HAM-110K, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset comprising more than 110,000 material structures covering 68 elements with both Hamiltonian and wavefunction data. Experiments on MP-HAM-110K and Materials-HAM-SOC demonstrate that DP-Learner dramatically improves Hamiltonian prediction accuracy and inference efficiency over the state-of-the-art method.

items.title: Quantum Metric and Nonlinear Hall Effect of Photons
items.summary: Using the path-integral formalism, we show that photons possess a nontrivial quantum metric in momentum space. We derive the semiclassical action and equations of motion by taking into account the quantum metric. In media with a spatially varying refractive index $n(\mathbf{x})$, the quantum metric induces a shift in the trajectory of light at second order in spatial gradients of $n$, whose transverse component may be regarded as a nonlinear Hall effect of light. The quantum metric also gives rise to corrections to photon propagation relevant to gravitational lensing in curved spacetime at second order in wavelength, including a gravitational nonlinear Hall effect arising from the interplay between the geometry of position space and that of momentum space.

items.title: Energy spectra and cascade in the spin turbulence of a driven spinor Bose-Einstein condensate
items.summary: We investigate the spin-interaction energy spectrum of spin turbulence in a driven spinor Bose-Einstein condensate. Continuous spin driving of a spin-1 condensate produces a nonequilibrium steady state with spatially fluctuating magnetization. We observe a power-law scaling consistent with the $-7/3$ exponent predicted for spin-wave turbulence, which persists across our full range of drive strengths despite substantial changes in the spectral anisotropy. After switching off the drive, we track the free-decay evolution and find evidence consistent with a direct cascade of spin-interaction energy toward higher wavenumbers. These results establish an energy-spectral hallmark of spin turbulence and enable quantitative studies of cascade dynamics in spinor superfluids.

items.title: Axial Thermal Transport in Transition Metal Chalcogenide Nanowires from Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations
items.summary: Transition metal chalcogenide M6X6 nanowires (M = Mo or W; X = S, Se, or Te) are promising one-dimensional (1D) building blocks for nanowire bundles and arrays, but how elemental composition controls their intrinsic axial heat transport remains unclear. Here we develop a multicomponent neuroevolution potential (NEP) from first-principles reference data and use homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations to quantify the thermal conductivity of six MX6 nanowires. The Mo6X6 series show a nonmonotonic composition dependence, whereas the thermal conductivity of the W6X6 series decreases monotonically with increasing chalcogen mass. Frequency-resolved thermal conductivity and phonon mean-free path analyses show that axial heat conduction is dominated by low-frequency phonons. Vibrational density of states and spectral energy density analyses further reveal that the contrasting trends arise from a competition between metal-chalcogen vibrational matching and phonon softening induced by heavier chalcogen atoms. A phenomenological model incorporating the combined atomic mass and the relative mass difference between the metal and chalcogen atoms reproduces these trends. These results link elemental composition, phonon characteristics and axial thermal conductivity in M6X6 nanowires, providing an atomistic basis for selecting heat-conducting units in nanowire bundles and arrays.

items.title: Type-IV 't Hooft Anomalies on the Lattice: Emergent Higher-Categorical Symmetries and Applications to LSM Systems
items.summary: 't Hooft anomalies impose fundamental constraints on quantum matter and often lead to emergent symmetry structures upon gauging. We analyze a lattice model with four global symmetries realizing a mixed anomaly described by $\sim a_1\wedge a_2\wedge a_3\wedge a_4$, where the $a_i$ denote background gauge fields for the global symmetries. Through explicit lattice gauging, we demonstrate the emergence of higher symmetry structures, including 2-group, non-invertible, and higher fusion categorical symmetries. We also provide a field theoretical understanding of these results. Applying this framework to systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis anomalies, obtained by promoting part of the internal symmetries to translational symmetries, we demonstrate that modulated (dipole) symmetries and non-invertible translation symmetry arise as direct counterparts of those in systems with purely internal type-IV anomalies. Importantly, we uncover a qualitatively new feature absent in previously studied modulated symmetries and non-invertible translation: their realization can become intrinsically defect-dependent. In particular, the emergent symmetry structure changes depending on whether symmetry defects are present. This work establishes a concrete lattice realization of mixed anomalies and reveals a rich structure of emergent symmetries, thereby clarifying their role in constraining quantum phases of matter.

items.title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
items.summary: A liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) exhibits a two-way coupling between its mesogen order and network elasticity: the mesogen order sets the undeformed network conformation, and the network deformation reorients the mesogens. This coupling gives rise to large, reversible stimuli-responsive actuation, as well as to soft elasticity, a finite deformation at nearly zero stress. This article reviews the elastic theory of ideal LCEs, bridging single-chain statistics and continuum constitutive models. The "ideal" elastic behavior rests on the assumption of anisotropic Gaussian chains that retain no memory of the crosslinking state, such that the director can rotate at no cost of free energy when accompanied by a corresponding stress-free, ground-state deformation. The resulting neo-classical free energy of a monodomain LCE, when minimized over the director, is non-quasi-convex, with a continuous family of stress-free ground states, leading to thermally induced spontaneous deformation and soft elasticity accommodated by coexisting stripe domains. The quasi-convex relaxation of the free energy classifies the behavior of polydomain LCEs into three phases, each with a distinct macroscopic mechanical response depending on the stretch state. The ideal elastic theory can be further extended to incorporate additional behaviors and physical processes, including thermo- and photomechanical coupling, Frank elasticity from director distortion, semi-soft or non-soft behavior arising from network nonideality, and temperature- and rate-dependent viscoelasticity.

items.title: Quantum order by disorder among lozenge tilings: a staircase of hub-free crystals between the Lieb ferrimagnet and the antiferromagnet
items.summary: Lozenge tilings of the triangular lattice define an exponentially large family of bipartite networks, from the dice lattice, a Lieb ferrimagnet with the largest sublattice imbalance, to square-type tilings, which are compensated antiferromagnets. For the classical Heisenberg antiferromagnet all of them are degenerate. We show that quantum fluctuations lift this degeneracy through a local mechanism: the zero-point energy is, to leading order, a sum of site terms that are convex in the coordination $z$, so that Jensen's inequality at fixed $\langle z\rangle=4$ selects the square-type tiling. An expansion about the Ising limit explains the convexity: a site with more bonds has more channels for quantum fluctuations, but each fluctuation frustrates more bonds. A magnetic field couples to the Lieb moment and competes with this selection. Because the moment is carried most cheaply by threefold and fivefold sites, sixfold hubs are avoided, and bond counting together with the Lieb--Mattis theorem limits hub-free tilings to $3/5$ of the dice moment. Quantum Monte Carlo and a complete enumeration of periodic tilings with small unit cells show that the classical jump is replaced by a staircase of periodic crystals. Its widest step is a hub-free crystal that saturates the bound; below it, threefold and fivefold defects pack ever more densely in a shallow sequence of crystals, controlled by a short-ranged attraction between defects of equal curvature and a repulsion between defects of opposite curvature. Selection energies scale as $JS$. In the height representation the coordination is the discrete Gaussian curvature and the Lieb moment its sublattice-staggered part. We give spectroscopic signatures and discuss realizations in nanographenes, atomic spin arrays and quantum simulators.

items.title: Growth and anisotropic directional dependent transport properties of Altermagnetic CrSb
items.summary: CrSb is a metallic altermagnet exhibiting large momentum-dependent spin splitting and antifer- romagnetic ordering well above room temperature. Although its electronic and magnetotransport properties have attracted considerable attention, a systematic comparison of crystals prepared us- ing different growth methods remains limited. Here we investigate the structural, magnetic, and anisotropic transport properties of CrSb single crystals grown by Sb(self)-flux, Bi flux, and chem- ical vapor transport (CVT). Each of these growth reveals distinct crystal morphologies. Magne- tization measurements exhibit broadly consistent antiferromagnetic responses, with an additional low-temperature contribution observed in Bi-flux-grown crystals. All samples display metallic resis- tivity and positive, nonsaturating magnetoresistance up to 9 T. Sb-flux- and CVT-grown crystals exhibit comparable residual resistivity ratios and magnetoresistance, whereas Bi-flux-grown crys- tals show enhanced residual resistivity and a substantially reduced magnetoresistance, consistent with stronger carrier scattering. Hall measurements reveal a pronounced dependence on the field- current configuration, including nonlinear field dependence and opposite Hall polarities for different crystallographic orientations. These results establish the reproducibility of anisotropic magneto- transport across distinct growth routes while highlighting the sensitivity of carrier scattering to crystal-growth conditions. Our findings provide a comparative framework for selecting CrSb single crystals for orientation-dependent transport and spintronic investigations.

items.title: Non-Abelian Quantum Turbulence in Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensates
items.summary: We numerically investigate statistically steady quantum turbulence in the cyclic phase of a spin-2 spinor Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) driven by large-scale energy injection via a divergence-free external velocity field. In the full non-Abelian cyclic system, the mass-current spectrum exhibits an anomalous $k^{-7/3}$ scaling, whereas the spin-current spectrum approximately follows a $k^{-5/3}$ power law. To isolate the role of non-Abelian vortex dynamics, we compare this system with an Abelian-restricted cyclic system sharing the same Hamiltonian parameters and driving conditions. Strikingly, the Abelian restriction collapses both the mass- and spin-current spectra into a single $k^{-5/3}$ scaling, identical to that of a scalar BEC, despite the three distinct turbulent states maintaining nearly identical vortex-line densities. A Helmholtz decomposition reveals that the mass- and spin-current spectra are predominantly incompressible and transverse, respectively, thereby confirming that the anomalous scaling cannot be attributed simply to compressible fluctuations or to the transverse nature of the energy injection. Local spectral exponents further quantify these distinct scaling regimes. The disappearance of the mass-spin spectral separation under the Abelian restriction, alongside the formation of a large-scale web of rung-connected non-Abelian vortices, provides compelling evidence that non-Abelian vortex dynamics fundamentally govern the organization of turbulent mass flow.

items.title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
items.summary: Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specially, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and exhibits long endurance comparable to the lifetime of synaptic proteins, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced in the identification of both greyscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.summary: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. The charge transition level is found at VBM$+$0.08~eV, conclusively ruling out the previously proposed association with the B3 EPR center and its correlated deep donor level. Most significantly, we identify a metastable spin-1 triplet excited state separated from the singlet by $\sim$1.6~meV, consistent with the NL51 EPR signal. The $D_{2d}$ symmetry of the defect suppresses intersystem crossing and phosphorescence by first-order spin--orbit coupling, implying an exceptionally long spin--lattice relaxation time. Combined with a spectrally resolvable zero-field splitting and near-infrared emission, the triplet state of the I$_4$ complex constitutes a viable spin quantum memory intrinsic to silicon.

items.title: Transition-Metal Substitutions in MOF-5: A Hybrid-DFT Study of Oxygen Electrocatalysis
items.summary: Hybrid density functional theory calculations were used to investigate the stability, electronic properties, and catalytic activity of transition-metal impurities substituting Zn sites (M\(_{\rm Zn}\)) in the MOF-5 metal-organic framework [Zn\(_4\)O(BDC)\(_3\), BDC = 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate], with M = Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu. Most substitutions introduce \(3d\) states within the MOF-5 band gap and induce localized magnetic moments. Partially occupied \(3d\) states promote orbital hybridization and charge transfer with oxygenated intermediates, activating the dopant sites toward oxygen electrocatalysis. The oxygen reduction and evolution reaction (ORR and OER) activities were evaluated using the computational hydrogen electrode model. Mn\(_{\rm Zn}\) and Fe\(_{\rm Zn}\) exhibit calculated ORR overpotentials of 0.57~V, while Mn\(_{\rm Zn}\) and Co\(_{\rm Zn}\) yield OER overpotentials of 0.42 and 0.51~V, respectively, approaching those of benchmark precious-metal electrocatalysts. These findings identify Mn substitution as a promising strategy for achieving bifunctional ORR/OER activity in MOF-5 and establish a link between dopant electronic structure and catalytic performance to guide the design of MOF-based electrocatalysts.

items.title: The spin-transfer inverse Faraday effect in Au/YIG thin film bilayers
items.summary: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) (the generation of an effective magnetic field in a material upon irradiation with circularly polarized light) offers a pathway to ultrafast, non-thermal control of spin dynamics. In metallic/ferromagnetic-insulator (NM/FMI) bilayers, IFE-driven spin polarization in the metallic layer can be an alternative to generate magnon excitations in the magnetic insulator which otherwise would be inaccessible with photon energies below the insulator bandgap, but this avenue has remained mostly unexplored. In this work, we investigate the regime of spin-transfer via IFE in Au/YIG bilayers, by means of ultrafast time-resolved magneto-optical experiments. Understanding the mechanism of this spin-transfer IFE in these NM/FMI heterostructures is crucial for several reasons: it elucidates the fundamental coupling between light's angular momentum and collective spin modes at buried interfaces, it enables all-optical generation and manipulation of pure spin currents, and it paves the way toward THz-frequency spintronic devices leveraging the insulator's long magnon lifetimes.

items.title: Augmenting Quantum Neural Networks with Contractive Layers
items.summary: Classical neural networks combine diverse layers with complementary roles to achieve rich expressive capabilities across complex learning tasks. Rapid advances in quantum science and technology have motivated growing interest in their quantum counterparts, quantum neural networks, raising the question of how their expressivity can be enhanced through the design of new quantum layers. Of particular interest are layers that enrich the accessible function space while introducing only a small number of additional trainable parameters. In this Letter, we introduce the contractive layer as a promising building block for quantum neural networks. This layer comprises all-to-all couplings governed by a single trainable parameter, enabling efficient control of quantum information flow while maintaining experimental relevance to Rydberg atom arrays. Using observable learning as a benchmark, we show that contractive layers enhance expressivity more efficiently than simply increasing the depth of conventional brick-wall circuits. This advantage stems from a systematic increase in the accessible target-space dimension per trainable parameter. We further demonstrate similar improvements in image recognition tasks. These results highlight contractive layers as a practical route to expressive quantum neural networks on near-term quantum devices.

items.title: Energy and Charge Transmission at Conformal Interfaces: Relations and Bounds
items.summary: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. For interfaces between Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models $G_{k_L}$ and $G_{k_R}$ preserving the diagonal affine algebra, we derive an exact relation between the energy and charge transmission coefficients, $c_{LR}=2(\dim G)k_{LR}/(k_L+k_R+2h^\vee)$. Together with positivity of outgoing energy, this relation excludes complete energy transmission at unequal levels. With additional bulk degrees of freedom, the equality is replaced by bounds controlled by the coset central charges. Complete transmission from a lower-level WZW model then imposes a lower bound on the coset central charge on the other side. In linear response, the relation fixes the ratio of thermal to charge conductance to the harmonic mean of the two bulk ratios, independently of the interface, while coset sectors bound the thermal conductance at fixed charge conductance. This interface-independent ratio is a generalized Wiedemann--Franz law for conformal interfaces between WZW models. The charge transmission coefficient $k_{LR}$ also governs equilibrium charge fluctuations and fixes the leading quadratic dependence of the boundary-condition-changing operator's scaling dimension on the rotation angle.

items.title: Generalized Critical-State Analysis of Local Field Screening in High-Pressure Yttrium Polyhydride
items.summary: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

items.title: Competing redox and material redistribution during electrode ageing
items.summary: Electrochemical processes can involve coupled redox reactions, active-material redistribution and morphological evolution at buried electrode-electrolyte interfaces1-3. Operando imaging has revealed nanoscale heterogeneity in these processes3-9, but how reversible redox and cumulative material redistribution interact during cycles to govern electrode ageing remains unclear. Here we develop fast operando soft X-ray spectro-ptychography to track oxidation state, morphology and iron redistribution in the same nanoscale region of an alkaline iron anode over 20 h of cycling. We distinguish two coexisting processes operating on different timescales. Within each cycle, iron undergoes rapid, reversible conversion between metallic iron and iron oxyhydroxide (FeOOH) with little net iron redistribution. Across cycles, slower iron redistribution, consistent with dissolution and redeposition, promotes FeOOH-rich particle growth. Particle-resolved trajectories reveal that reversible conversion and iron accumulation coexist within individual particles, while particles with similar apparent growth exhibit markedly different changes in iron content. Local capacity initially increases as particles grow, then declines as more iron remains oxidized after charging and the reversible redox swing narrows. These findings suggest that cumulative Fe redistribution competes with reversible redox by progressively limiting the Fe available for charge storage. More generally, electrode ageing can begin during nearly reversible cycling, before capacity loss becomes apparent.

items.title: Unveiling plastic rearrangements in silica glass through persistent homology
items.summary: Plastic deformation of amorphous solids proceeds through localised atomic rearrangements. While much effort has been devoted to identifying where such rearrangements occur, how the local structure changes during a rearrangement is less well understood. In silica glass, a rearrangement can involve both distortion within SiO4 tetrahedra and deformation of the network connecting them, but the contributions of these two modes have rarely been quantified. Here, we characterise plastic rearrangements in silica glass under athermal quasistatic shear using persistent homology, which extracts rings from atomic configurations, and link the changes in the persistence diagrams to individual rings in real space. We classify rearrangement events into two types according to bond-coordination changes. By performing inverse analysis, we reveal that Si-centred triangles within tetrahedra, hinge triangles spanning two corner-sharing tetrahedra, and the other (non-hinge) O3 triangles are the dominant sources of topological changes upon rearrangements. The birth-time changes of Si-centred and hinge triangles closely follow the change in the angle opposite the longest edge, whereas that of non-hinge triangles also reflects changes in inter-tetrahedral O--O distances. Further, we clarify that triangles with large birth-time changes are localised in the rearrangement region. Comparing the two types of triangles, we find that the ratio of their birth-time changes is larger for coordination-changing events than for coordination-preserving events, indicating that such events involve relatively more intra-tetrahedral deformation compared with network deformation. These results demonstrate that persistent homology separates intra-tetrahedral and network deformation and quantifies each as a continuous quantity within a single framework.

items.title: Resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in one-dimensional quantum scattering
items.summary: We study resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in a one-dimensional quantum-scattering model. Two incoming electrons scatter independently from a symmetric double-barrier structure and the sector with one reflected and one transmitted electron is selected. The idealised delta-function barriers used in earlier work are replaced by exponentially localised cusp barriers, $U(x)=U_0\exp(-|x\mp d/2|/a)$, for which the single-barrier scattering problem is exactly solvable in terms of modified Bessel functions of imaginary order. We derive the corresponding reflection and transmission amplitudes, verify their current normalisation and validate them independently by direct numerical integration. Two separated cusp barriers are then combined through a Fabry-Pérot composition, whose accuracy is quantified by solving the full two-centre Schrödinger equation. In the well-separated regime the approximation reproduces the full resonance positions to high accuracy. The concurrence zeros are controlled by the resonance phase condition $δ(κ)+κd=nπ$, with a continuously unwrapped single-barrier reflection phase $δ$. We also calculate the post-selection probability $P_{RT}$, showing explicitly that large conditional concurrence can occur in a low-probability sector. Systematic scans in barrier width, integrated strength and reference momentum show that finite width can shift off-resonant concurrence maxima and, depending on the reference momentum, reduce their attainable height. The results identify resonance-controlled conditional entanglement as a robust feature of the well-separated double-barrier geometry rather than an artefact of the zero-range idealisation.

items.title: High-Sensitivity Magnetometry with Scalable Mixed SQUID Arrays
items.summary: The utilisation of Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUIDs), a loop of superconducting material hosting two Josephson junctions, has long been at the forefront of quantum sensing. To enhance performance and signal power, modern architectures connect multiple SQUIDs into two-dimensional series-parallel arrays called Superconducting Quantum Interference Filters (SQIFs). A major recent advancement, called a mixed-SQUID array, integrates junction-free ``bare" loops alongside active SQUID loops, offering a promising strategy to engineer high-performance alternatives to traditional SQIF technology. However, a rigorous theoretical optimization and performance scaling analysis for this novel geometry remains lacking. In this work, an analytical framework, validated against full numerical simulations, is developed to establish fundamental design rules for this technology. This work systematically examines how key quantum sensing parameters evolve as a function of loop inductance, parasitic coupling, and overall array dimensions. Crucially, it is demonstrated that these mixed SQUID arrays circumvent the severe inductive screening losses inherent to conventional SQIF designs, achieving a performance boost in flux sensitivity in the range of $2-4\:\times$ under realistic device parameters.

items.title: Parametric excitation of nano-scale spin waves with controlled phase by an open-resonator-type transducer
items.summary: Parametric excitation is one of the most effective methods for the excitation of nano-scale spin waves (SW) (or magnons) in magnetic films and nano-waveguides, as this method removes restrictions on the excited wave wavelength imposed by a finite width of the excitation transducer. Especially efficient parametric excitation of SW is achieved if the SW excitation is based on the effect of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA). However, in a traditional parametric excitation process, the excited propagating waves have an arbitrary phase, which prevents the use of such waves in signal processing applications. Here, we demonstrate that the use of an VCMA transducer in the form of an open resonator with controlled partial reflections of waves at the boundaries allows one to excite SW having only two allowed phase states, controlled by the phase of the parametric pumping and reflections at the transducer boundaries. These reflections, also, lead to a reduced value of the parametric excitation threshold. In addition, micromagnetic simulations reveal the possibility to tune the phase distribution of the excited magnons using static voltage, which could be useful for applications in probabilistic computing.
