items.title: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys
items.summary: Nature Materials, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02801-5 Machine learning guides the design of an additively manufactured titanium alloy containing superfine features at the 10 nm scale through controlled martensitic transformation, which achieves an ultimate tensile strength of more than 1.7 GPa and 7.5% uniform elongation.

items.title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
items.summary: Nature Materials, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02813-1 All-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries are a next-generation high-energy-density solution for energy storage. Here catholyte/cathode interfaces are found to be as important as transport tortuosity in thick sulfur cathodes, and an areal capacity of 10 mAh cm−2 is demonstrated at a stack pressure of 15 MPa and sulfur loading of 6.1 mg cm−2.

items.title: Tracking local chemomechanics in graphite–silicon composite electrodes
items.summary: Nature Nanotechnology, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41565-026-02328-5 Operando 4D imaging reveals how local ionic pathways govern activity in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

items.title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
items.summary: Nature Nanotechnology, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41565-026-02327-6 Particle-resolved 4D nano-tomography identifies fast ionic transport pathways as key regulators of electrochemical activity and reversibility in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

items.title: Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
items.summary: Nature Nanotechnology, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41565-026-02330-x A bilayer meta-atom structure engineers the antireflective capabilities of the metasurface, without affecting its full 0–2π transmission phase coverage.

items.title: Laser intensity control over ionization asymmetry of hydrogen atom with a synthesized ω –...
authors: Ming-Qiang Fu, Hong-Bin Yao, Zhao-Peng Sun, Ming-jing Bian, Chang-hong Cao, Talgar Shaymurat, Bumaliya Abulimiti and Bei Zhang
items.summary: The ionization asymmetry of hydrogen atom in a synthesized 400–800 nm laser field is investigated by numerically solving the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation. The left-right asymmetry of the threshold peak exhibits multiple reversals with the increasing 800 nm laser intensity. The photoelectron momentum distributions show that the addition of 800 nm field leads to increasingly complex interference structures. By analyzing the partial-wave-resolved photoelectron energy spectra and coherent odd–even partial-wave pair contributions, we show that the repeated asymmetry reversals originate from the intensity-dependent redistribution of the contributing partial-wave components and the resulting changes in odd–even partial-wave interference. The accompanying redistribution of the projected excited-state populations is consistent with intensity-dependent changes in the effective multiphoton resonance conditions. The combined population and continuum analyses support a qualitative picture in which varying the 800 nm intensity redistributes the relative contributions of excitation and ionization pathways, thereby reshaping the outgoing partial-wave composition. This partial-wave interference picture provides important insight into multiphoton ionization dynamics and offers a route for coherent control of photoionization asymmetry in atomic and molecular systems.

items.title: The CISS effect as a case of emergent magnetization at metal-molecule interfaces
authors: Oliver L.A. Monti, Amos Sharoni, Yonatan Dubi
items.summary: Chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) has long been regarded as a magnetic effect unique to chiral molecules, yet it shares the same metal-molecule systems as the decades-old phenomenon of emergent magnetism at interfaces. Monti et al. present evidence that CISS is a special case of this interfacial magnetization, arguing that chirality acts as a “director” that aligns an otherwise delicate, pre-existing magnetic signal with the measurement geometry—the first proposed link between these two fields.

items.title: Flux Jamming and Bimodal Dynamics in Bounded Spin Networks
items.summary: Finite-sized frustrated magnetic networks relax through pathways that are strongly shaped by their boundaries; yet, whether their kinetic barriers can be predicted from geometry alone has remained unclear. Here, we present a transfer matrix framework for finite artificial square ice that links local coordination to the effective energy landscape and the temperature-dependent barriers governing magnetic flux transport. By combining nonhomogeneous transfer matrices with the local coordination hierarchy, we identify the geometric bottlenecks that govern the relaxation dynamics, and show that the leading steady-state weight falls on charge-neutral, ice-rule configurations, which are thermodynamically preferred due to their reduced electrostatic energy and greater configurational multiplicity. The resulting two time-scale structure suggests bimodal behavior: (1) long intervals of trapping in charge-compensated manifolds are interrupted by (2) sudden avalanche-like relaxation events. Applied to Husimi-tree representations, the framework yields a low-temperature initial arrest probability that collapses across forty generations onto a common scaling function of $g-ξ(T)$, with a crossover length $ξ\sim T^{-ν}$ and $ν=1$. These results show that boundary geometry alone can produce kinetic arrest and suggest intermittent transport, even in the absence of quenched disorder, reminiscent of athermal granular jamming. More broadly, our framework connects the coordination landscape, equilibrium energetics, and nonequilibrium relaxation in finite frustrated magnets and provides a route to understanding boundary-controlled dynamics in artificial spin ice.

items.title: Interfacial Transition Waves and Domain Wall Self-Pinning in Bi-stable Mechanical Metamaterial
items.summary: The understanding of transition waves in mechanical metamaterials currently derives from architectures fitting one of three archetypes as distinguished by the stability and order parameter: multi-stable with scalar or vector order parameter, and bi-stable with scalar order parameter. However, a fourth archetype is conspicuously absent: bi-stable with vector order parameter. Completing the tetrad, in this article, we numerically examine the transformation dynamics unique to bi-stable mechanical metamaterials with vector order parameter. We report two types of interfacial transition waves, whose propagation is restricted to the narrow region of configurational boundaries (e.g., domain walls). We show that the wave speed may depend on its polarization. In addition, we reveal an approach to regulate the severity of discreteness effects, which elevates discreteness as an intrinsic, tunable mechanism for controlling the wave speed -- including pinning/de-pinning of the domain wall -- without altering the metamaterial architecture. The results support applications in, e.g., reconfigurable mechanical circuits and complex domain patterning, and motivate further investigation of metamaterials with unconventional transition processes.

items.title: Majorana quasiparticles, mass hierarchies, and the phase diagram of the Gross-Neveu model in D=2+1
items.summary: We show that the canonical $2+1$-dimensional $O(2N)$-symmetric Gross-Neveu model with the inversion-breaking mass-term features a sequence of $O(2N-k) \times O(k)$ - symmetric ground states in its zero-temperature phase diagram, with $k=1,...,N$. For odd $k$ the quasiparticle excitations are itinerant, massive, two-real-component Majorana fermions, i.e. half of Dirac fermions. The solutions of the mean-field equations symmetric under $O(2N-k_1-k_2) \times O(k_1) \times O(k_2)$ with $k_1, k_2 \geq 1$ also exist, but are found to be unstable. Some manifestations of Majorana quasiparticle in the particular ``uniaxial nematic" state with $k=1$ are outlined, and analogies to other physical systems are offered.

items.title: First-principles-based Prediction of Phase Fields: Part II. Solid Solution Tunability in Refractory Complex Concentrated Alloys
items.summary: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCAs) offer a high-dimensional composition space for designing either robust single-phase solid solutions or controlled multiphase microstructures. However, most RCCA studies have examined isolated compositions, often near the equimolar point, rather than determining how solid-solution stability varies across the surrounding composition space. Here, we use rapid thermodynamic phase-field calculations to map the topology of solid-solution stability in RCCAs composed of Cr, Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, V, W, and Zr. Benchmarking the model against 109 experimentally reported quaternary-to-senary compositions produced through diverse processing routes yields an overall classification accuracy of 80%. We then introduce percentage miscible region, a metric that separates robust solid-solution-forming systems from those exhibiting compositionally tunable microstructures. Analysis of ternary, quaternary, and quinary RCCAs reveals that higher-order miscibility is strongly inherited from constituent binary subsystems, indicating the importance of choosing suitable binary interactions when designing RCCAs. Element-specific trends further show that Ti, Ta, Nb, and Mo generally stabilize solid solutions, whereas Cr and Zr promote ordered precipitation and phase segregation. Hf, W, and V, meanwhile, enable tuning between these regimes. These results establish a composition-space framework for the targeted design of RCCAs with robust solid-solution stability or tunable multiphase microstructures.

items.title: Artificial Spin-Glass of Antiferromagnetic Co3O4 Nanocubes Using Spin-Polarized Oxygen
items.summary: Preferentially exposing (100) surface terminations of Co$_{3}$O$_{4}$ using cube-shaped nanoparticles yields an unconventional rearrangement of ions that generates spin-glass-like magnetism from the antiferromagnetic nanocubes. The necessary magnetic frustration arises out of competition between polarized Co-O bonds from charge transfer between O 2p and Co 3d orbitals, and highly anisotropic Co$^{2+}$ ions combined with anomalous high spin Co$^{3+}$ ions in octahedral sites. Size control permits tuning this novel combination of ions via preferentially polarizing Co-O bonds. The presence of control over frustrated magnetism among antiferromagnetic nanocubes yields an artificial spin glass platform for exploring unconventional nanomagnetism and engendering new opportunities for emerging technologies like spintronics and physical reservoir computing.

items.title: Strain and Correlation Modulated Magnetic Anisotropy and Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya Interaction in 2D H-FeTe$_2$
items.summary: In the ongoing research on two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnetic materials with strong intrinsic Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction (DMI), most efforts have focused on doping, Janus engineering, or heterostructure formation to break inversion symmetry and enhance spin--orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we demonstrate that a pristine 2D material, monolayer H-FeTe$_2$, can naturally host robust DMI and magnetic anisotropy due to its intrinsic broken inversion symmetry and the strong SOC of Te atoms. We explore the effect of biaxial strain and electron correlation on H-FeTe$_2$ using first-principles DFT+$U$ calculations. We systematically investigate the Heisenberg exchange interaction, magnetic anisotropy, and DMI in the space spanned by strain and correlation. Our results reveal a distinct, non-monotonic strain dependence of both magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) and DMI, including a strain-tunable crossover between in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic easy axes. A remarkable enhancement of the in-plane DMI is observed under the combined influence of strain and strong correlations, which is unusual for pristine 2D materials and suggests a favorable regime for spintronic applications.Notably, even in the absence of strain, H-FeTe$_2$ exhibits finite DMI and considerable anisotropy, which is rare for a pure 2D material. Through these findings, we present H-FeTe$_2$ as a unique pristine 2D system with robust and tunable spin interactions for exploring fundamental spin--orbit-driven magnetic phenomena.

items.title: Geometric Contribution to the Electron-Phonon Coupling Constant: Checkerboard and Hyper-diamond Models
items.summary: Recent theoretical studies on electron-phonon coupling (EPC) - a key ingredient in the emergence of diverse quantum phases such as superconductivity and charge-density waves - have revealed a distinct contribution to its strength arising from the quantum geometry of electronic bands. Here we investigate the quantum geometric contribution, characterized by the quantum metric, to the dimensionless EPC constant in the checkerboard and hyper-diamond models, under the Gaussian approximation. We show that in the checkerboard model, the geometric contribution can be tuned independently while keeping the energetic part fixed, demonstrating the possibility of enhancing EPC strength through quantum geometry. In the hyper-diamond model, the geometric contribution accounts for roughly $50\%$ of the total EPC constant across all spatial dimensions, generalizing the $d=2$ result for graphene to higher dimensions.

items.title: Spin Space Symmetry Without Spin Space Groups
items.summary: Spin space groups provide a complete symmetry classification of magnetic structures in the non-relativistic limit. Each spin space group with a given parent space group is specified, up to spin-only symmetries, by a real representation of that space group acting in spin space. We argue that working directly with this representation not only avoids the construction and identification of the group, but also organizes and simplifies the resulting symmetry constraints on allowed responses. The presence or absence of magnetic compensation, piezomagnetism, spin and charge transport, the Edelstein effect, and momentum-space spin textures becomes an ordinary problem in the representation theory of space groups. The conditions reduce to overlaps between the three exterior powers of the defining representation and multipole representations of the point group. Several physically distinct responses then reduce to the same condition: a $p$-wave spin texture and the time-even Edelstein effect are allowed together, as are piezomagnetism and a $d$-wave spin texture in compensated order. The wave-vector content of the exterior powers gives a hierarchy of selection rules: depending on the power, a uniform response requires one, two, or three ordering wave vectors to sum to a reciprocal lattice vector. A non-relativistic anomalous Hall effect in compensated order at zero wave vector requires a defining representation built from three one-dimensional irreducible representations, a purely odd-parity spin texture requires a pair of nonzero ordering wave vectors that cancel, and coplanar order at nonzero wave vector in the interior of the Brillouin zone is always a $p$-wave magnet. We illustrate the approach with collinear, coplanar and non-coplanar magnets, and discuss extensions to magnetic space groups, connections to Landau theories of collinear order, and the characterization of odd-parity magnets.

items.title: Simple Routes to Turing-Like Patterns
items.summary: Spots, stripes, and networks recur in systems with very different microscopic dynamics, suggesting that the competing processes behind Turing-like patterns may be easy to realise. We ask whether local amplification coupled to suppression over a wider region can generate these geometries in simple systems beyond chemical reaction--diffusion models. We test this idea in two settings, a binary cellular automaton obtained by adding a distant neighbour count to Conway's Game of Life and a self-gravitating toy universe described by particle motion and two continuous fields. The automaton produces spots, stripes, and coexistence across its control plane, while a rule retaining only the two opposing counts produces islands, stripes, and holes. Directional correlations and intrinsic dimension identify the same region of orientational order. In the gravitational system, convergence increases local density while mass transport depletes the surroundings. The two-field and particle densities have a smoothed spatial correlation of $0.962$ at scale factor $a=1$ under the original force law, and strengthening its long-wavelength component drives both descriptions toward fewer dense condensations. Together, these results show how simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realise competing growth and suppression, providing two concrete routes by which Turing-like geometries can recur across different dynamics.

items.title: Tuning the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in CoFeB thin film heterostructures
items.summary: The Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI) is essential for stabilizing chiral spin textures in spintronics, yet achieving consistent quantitative measurements across different techniques remains a significant challenge. Heterostructures consisting of magnetic thin films sandwiched between non-magnetic heavy metals have been shown to possess substantial DMI; however, these vary in both magnitude and handedness for supposedly identical samples, indicating the sensitivity of DMI to both interfacial properties and measurement techniques. Here, systematic tuning of the DMI in ultra-thin magnetic heterostructures of Pt/CoFeB/Ta/Pt is achieved by varying the thickness of a tantalum sub-monolayer with thicknesses ranging from $0.1\,\mathrm{nm}$ to $0.4\,\mathrm{nm}$. The magnitude and sign of the DMI are measured using three independent methods: the parallel stripe domain model, edge nucleation field analysis, and Brillouin light scattering. The three independent approaches reveal excellent agreement within the experimental error. This ability to controllably tune and reliably quantify DMI provides a viable route toward engineering chiral magnetic textures, including domain walls and skyrmions, for next-generation spintronic devices. The necessity for precise measurements of magnetic parameters and careful attention to detail are discussed because calculations of the DMI for each technique depend on different parameters.

items.title: 2D Transport in an in-plane magnetic field
items.summary: A parallel in-plane magnetic field could, in principle, distinguish between two competing physical scenarios for the experimentally observed density-tuned 2D metal-insulator transition (where decreasing the carrier density leads to a crossover from an effective metal to an effective insulator): Wigner crystallization or Anderson localization. Since the main scattering mechanism in 2D doped semiconductors arises from screened random charged impurities and screening in turn depends on the electronic density of states, the in-plane magnetic field could distinguish between the two by decreasing screening through spin polarization and this enhances the effective critical density for Anderson localization compared with Wigner crystallization. We give the general theory and provide results for the quantitative magnitudes of the spin polarization effect on the transition density by focusing on two recent experiments [Z. Ge, et al, Nature (London) 654, 902 (2026), T. Han, et al, arXiv:2604.00113], noting that the critical density may actually decrease if the dominant scattering is by short-ranged defects instead of long-ranged charged impurities. The difference between the two cases arises from whether spin polarization dominates screening (enhanced critical density) or the Fermi surface (suppressed critical density).

items.title: Logical qubits with geometrically enhanced energetic and parametric protection
items.summary: Breaking the error-threshold marks a milestone in establishing quantum advantage for a wide range of relevant problems. One possible route is to encode information redundantly in a logical qubit by combining several noisy qubits, providing an increased robustness against external perturbations. We propose a setup for a logical qubit in a generalized Tavis-Cummings model consisting of physical qubits coupled to a logical all-to-one element. Our design is based on a recently discovered geometric stabilizing mechanism in the closely related Bose-Hubbard wheel, which manifests as energetically well-separated clusters of many-body eigenstates. We show that even in the presence of typical fabrication uncertainties, their occurrence and separation is extremely robust. Introducing an additional physical qubit coupled to the central element yields replicas of these clusters, for which we introduce two prototypical coupling schemes. (i) A local coupling protocol exploits the spectral separation to encode information redundantly. (ii) A non-local coupling protocol additionally generates a symmetry-protected operating point at which virtual transitions produce no leading-order differential energy shift within the logical manifold. Our results establish geometrically stabilized many-body spectral clusters as tools to construct logical qubit manifolds with independently tunable energetic and parametric error protection.

items.title: Memory kernel and closure for systems driven by intermittent forcing with power-law waiting times
items.summary: Many systems are driven by an intermittent forcing that takes on a random value for a random time interval. For such renewal step noise, the master equation for the driven variable has a memory kernel whose coefficients are the totally time-ordered cumulants, or $G$-cumulants, of the noise. In the case of Poisson switching, these correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the jump distribution, and the kernel can be summed exactly. We derive an exact decomposition of these coefficients for any waiting-time distribution with independent amplitudes and durations, which separates the jump statistics from the renewal statistics. For power-law waiting-time densities, $ψ(θ)\proptoθ^{-μ}$ with $μ>2$ (finite mean), a long time interval is most likely covered by a single epoch, and we prove that, as a result, the coefficients cross over at long lags, at all orders, from the Boolean cumulants to the ordinary moments of the jump law. The long-lag kernel thus becomes a superposition of the kernels of the frozen deterministic flows, weighted by $ξ^2p(ξ)$, and the corresponding master equation follows in closed form. For $2<μ<3$, where the noise correlation time is infinite, the second-order closure retains a finite error even for slow dynamics, whereas the frozen-flow master equation yields the exact stationary mean in that limit. The telegraph process is the only renewal step noise for which the second-order closure is exact. An exactly solvable model with correlated additive and multiplicative noise confirms these predictions.

items.title: Infection Spreading and Stochastic Extinction in Finite Spatially Inhomogeneous Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible and Susceptible-Infected-Recovered Systems
items.summary: Demographic fluctuations can drive finite epidemic populations into an absorbing disease-free state even when the corresponding infinite system supports sustained activity. By means of Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate how spatial coupling of two distinct subsystems modifies stochastic extinction and epidemic spreading in susceptible-infectious-susceptible (SIS) and susceptible-infectious-recovered (SIR) models on inhomogeneous two-dimensional square lattices. For isolated SIS systems, extinction times exhibit approximate power-law scaling near the epidemic threshold even for small systems. Traversal times characterize the distinct propagation dynamics of SIS and SIR infection clusters. We consider diffusively coupled regions with different transmission characteristics in coupled SIS-SIS, SIR-SIS, and SIR-SIR configurations. Invading fronts can reactivate a vulnerable SIS region after its initial infection has disappeared and establish a long-lived active epidemic state. This stabilization can be induced by either a sustained SIS source or a single transient SIR epidemic wave. Spatial correlation measurements support a mechanism in which the invading activity generates an extended correlated infectious population, effectively providing favorable initial conditions for renewed epidemic spreading. Correlations develop particularly strongly parallel to the subsystem interfaces. Decoupling the regions after some elapsed period demonstrates that autonomous persistence requires sufficient coupling time beyond the first interface arrival for this correlated population to become established. Increasing system size delays invasion but enhances the probability of ultimate successful stabilization. In two coupled SIR regions, transmission can initiate a macroscopic secondary outbreak, while permanent immunity restricts both epidemics to transient activity.

items.title: Prediction of lattice thermal conductivity of half-Heusler compounds by machine learning and transfer-function calibration
items.summary: High-throughput searches for half-Heusler thermoelectrics increasingly rely on lattice thermal conductivity ($κ_L$) from first-principles calculations, or from machine-learning models trained on them. These calculations describe an ideal single crystal, whereas measurements are made on polycrystalline samples, in which grain boundaries and defects scatter heat as well. The resulting gap between calculated and measured $κ_L$ has been noted for individual compounds but not, to our knowledge, quantified across a materials class, so the values used for screening carry an unknown, systematic bias. Here we quantify and correct this bias for cubic half-Heusler compounds with 18 valence electrons. Using a curated literature corpus that keeps calculated and measured values apart, we show that calculations overestimate measured $κ_L$ in most bonding families, and that the excess shrinks with temperature. Scattering by defects, added to the intrinsic scattering between lattice vibrations, would give such a trend, but the data do not single out one cause. A simple transfer function with this temperature dependence removes the median offset, and refitting its magnitude within a bonding family lowers the median error further, though not consistently compound by compound. Combined with a machine-learning model that predicts the calculated value from crystal structure, and tested on chemistries withheld from all fitting, the method predicts measured $κ_L$ in this class about as closely as independent laboratories agree with one another, and provides testable predictions for compounds not yet measured.

items.title: Geometric properties of Wilsonian flows of periodic potentials in two dimensions
items.summary: Periodic interactions can possess multiple competing minima and barriers, whose evolution under coarse-graining offers a geometric perspective complementary to the scaling of Fourier harmonics. We study this evolution in two dimensions by deriving a functional Wilsonian renormalization-group flow for a general smooth periodic potential and its running sine-Gordon frequency within a constant-kinetic projection. Reaction--diffusion and Burgers representations reveal two key properties of the flow: discrete translation symmetries are preserved, and the number of extrema can only remain constant or decrease. Consequently, the nonlinear generation of Fourier harmonics may accompany a progressive simplification of the potential landscape. We illustrate the role of symmetry with two complementary examples. A weak breaking of the $π$-translation symmetry allows a reduction from four extrema to two, whereas a non-sinusoidal interaction retaining this symmetry evolves from eight extrema to the four protected by its periodicity. These results highlight how symmetry and coarse-graining jointly reorganize competing minima and barriers in periodic interactions.

items.title: Fully Automated Discovery of Phase Diagrams Using Agentic Large Language Models
items.summary: Classifying phases of matter and mapping out phase diagrams are central problems in physics. Recently, machine learning techniques have emerged as promising tools for phase classification, ranging from supervised learning to various unsupervised methods. However, these techniques provide limited qualitative insight into the discovered phases, typically work only for specific system classes, and do not by themselves efficiently map out the phase diagram. Autonomously constructing the phase diagram of a general system purely from measurements, without prior knowledge of the system, while also yielding qualitative understanding of the phases, remains an open task. In this work, we introduce Phasonaut, a two-agent framework that leverages the tool-use capabilities and broad knowledge of large language models (LLMs) to drive an active learning loop that constructs phase diagrams of physical systems and provides interpretations of the discovered phases. Starting from scratch, it iteratively selects and performs measurements, analyzes the resulting data, and segments the parameter domain into the phases it discovers. Phasonaut recovers the phase diagrams of classical and quantum spin systems to substantial precision. In the future, this framework could enable rapid exploration of systems with unknown phase diagrams, including in autonomously driven experiments.

items.title: Emergent Long-Range Entanglement in the XXZ Quantum Spin Chain with Competing Orders
items.summary: Competition between short-range and long-range interactions is a largely unexplored route to one-dimensional quantum matter. We introduce a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour and antiferromagnetic power-law couplings. Using DMRG and spin-wave theory, we show this competition stabilises a gapless phase with central charge $c=0.997(17)$, a twofold-degenerate ground state and entanglement spectrum, absent in nearest-neighbour models, and is long-range entangled as diagnosed by finite quantum conditional mutual information. The model also generates a unique gapped quantum phase and gapless antiphase with non-decaying correlations.

items.title: Large Dense Thermodynamic Networks Nearly Minimize Entropy Production
items.summary: Many have speculated whether nonequilibrium systems obey principles of maximum or minimum entropy production. In this work, we use stochastic thermodynamics to derive the condition for the minimum entropy production state (MEPS) for continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs), even far from equilibrium. We show that real nonequilibrium steady states (NESS) generally violate both the Minimum and Maximum Entropy Production (MINEP and MAXEP) principles. However, through numerical sampling of large densely-connected CTMCs, we find that as system size increases, the steady-state entropy production tends to converge to a value close to the minimum. By contrast, sparsely-connected thermodynamic networks become less efficient. This suggests that large dense nonequilibrium networks may self-organize to use thermodynamic resources efficiently, offering a nuanced perspective on the longstanding debate between MAXEP and MINEP.

items.title: Atomic layer etching of niobium via alternating O$_2$ and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures
items.summary: Niobium thin films are a key component of superconducting detectors and electronics, and film surface quality, surface roughness, and geometrical dimensional accuracy affect many performance metrics. Atomic layer etching (ALE) is of interest for modifying film surfaces owing to its Angstrom-scale etching precision and surface smoothing characteristics. Here, we report a plasma-enhanced ALE process for Nb based on sequential O$_2$ plasma and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures. The process achieves an etch per cycle of 5-7 Angstrom/cycle and exhibits surface smoothing. The superconducting transition temperature of the ALE-treated films is maintained up to the expected decrease associated with reduced film thickness. Our ALE process could find applications in superconducting electronics for which surface quality and precise thickness control are of high importance.

items.title: Impact of spin fluctuations on spectral functions and transport in a model altermagnet
items.summary: Understanding spin dependent transport in altermagnets is important for incorporating them in next generation spintronic technologies. Motivated by the discovery of altermagnetism in strongly correlated quantum materials, we explore this physics in the checkerboard lattice Hubbard model using a fermion Monte Carlo approach which tracks the full spatial dependence of spin fluctuations as a function of temperature. We present results for the evolution of the spin-dependent single particle spectral functions and transport as we go from the ordered ground state into the high temperature disordered paramagnetic phase. Our results could be tested in future spin-selective angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin transport experiments in candidate altermagnets realized in solid state quantum materials or in proposed ultracold atomic systems.

items.title: Free-Space Excitation of Frozen Waves and Topological Edge States in Graphene at a Time Interface
items.summary: Time-varying two-dimensional materials, such as graphene under ultrafast photoexcitation, offer a promising platform for engineering temporal interfaces for electromagnetic waves. Rapidly promoting valence electrons to the conduction band generates a high-energy, non-thermal hot-electron population that subsequently thermalizes with the pre-existing thermal electron population. We study the excitation of plasmonic modes in graphene by the time interface created by ultra-fast photoexcitation using a graphene electron-transport model that is self-consistently coupled to electromagnetic simulations. We find that in addition to dynamic, propagating plasmonic modes, the time interfaces result in the excitation of static, spatially varying electromagnetic modes in the interaction region sustained by streaming transverse electrons. We also demonstrate a novel technique for coupling free-space light directly to highly localized topological edge states at the magnetic-inversion boundary on graphene, eliminating the need for near-field excitation techniques.

items.title: Passive Entropy Rate Bounds the Information Required for Feedback Control
items.summary: Living organisms across scales, along with many engineered devices, must control noisy systems with limited information to maintain a desired steady state. Here we ask how the performance of a feedback controller is limited by the rate at which information flows from sensors to control actions. We demonstrate that the minimum information rate required is the rate at which the passive dynamics increase the system's entropy. This general result allows us to quantify the information required to achieve a given target performance for a wide-ranging set of control problems. Next, we ask what explicit control protocol maximizes performance for a given information rate. We demonstrate that in many cases the best control strategy is to probabilistically time-reverse the uncontrolled passive dynamics. Implementing this protocol approaches or saturates our bound across a wide range of applications. We showcase these results through applications to stochastic bit control, nonlinear particle localization, microbial navigation, and experimentally realized information engines. Our findings pave the way for the study of feedback control in any settings where limited information is a key constraint, suggest principled explanations for microbial behavior, and provide new insights into fundamental questions regarding the thermodynamic value of information.

items.title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
items.summary: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.

items.title: When the magnetic force theorem fails: dressed exchange in the induced-moment magnets FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd
items.summary: Effective spin Hamiltonians for itinerant magnets are commonly parameterized by magnetic-force-theorem (MFT) exchange constants, which are subsequently used to compute the behavior of complex and delicate spin textures, for example skyrmions. We show that for systems containing atoms with large spin susceptibility, such as Pd or Pt, this approach misses important parts of the energetics. For FePt, it even predicts the wrong ground state. Benchmarking against fully self-consistent spin-spiral density-functional calculations - in which the electronic structure, including the induced Pd/Pt moments, relaxes for every spin configuration - we quantify the missing energetics for the ordered L1$_0$ alloys FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd. By comparing a family of models that differ only in their treatment of the induced Pt moment, including the configuration-dependent models of Mryasov and Polesya, we identify the origin: the energetics of the induced moments are governed by the exchange-enhanced (dressed) susceptibility, of which the frozen-potential MFT captures only the bare part - about one third of the Pt-mediated interaction in FePt. We derive a general bound showing that no on-site (intra-atomic) refinement can supply the missing strength. The dressing decides the magnetic ground state in FePt, where the interlayer ordering rests entirely on the Pt-mediated interactions, and shifts the Curie temperatures of the other alloys by several hundred kelvin. Computed ordering temperatures, magnon spectra and spin wave stiffness for all four compounds are provided.

items.title: Thermalization and quantum chaos in a pure gauge discrete non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
items.summary: Gauge theories constitute the basis of our microscopic description of fundamental physical laws, and they are a cornerstone of contemporary scientific research. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. In this work, we investigate the thermalization properties of non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, focusing on the discrete gauge group $D_3$, which is ideally suited for current qudit-based quantum simulators. Specifically, we study a linear plaquette chain in a gauge-fixed formulation that removes unphysical degrees of freedom. A numerical analysis of the Hamiltonian spectrum and expectation values of local operators shows a behavior broadly aligned with the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH). We also study thermalization through the real-time dynamics of the entanglement spectrum, confirming the emergence of random-matrix level statistics after an initial transient. Our results expand the rich phenomenology of dihedral non-Abelian gauge systems. Once the relevant symmetry structure is properly resolved, the model displays the same qualitative ETH-based thermalization scenario observed in Abelian gauge models and generic non-integrable quantum many-body systems.

items.title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
items.summary: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as $PHP=0$, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.

items.title: Off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing in one dimension from critical density fluctuations
items.summary: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have a destabilizing effect on superconductivity, by suppressing long-range order or by destroying Fermi-liquid quasiparticles in the normal state. In this work, we study a one-dimensional (1D) model of spinless fermions with local interactions that exhibits a continuous quantum phase transition from a Luttinger liquid to a phase-separated state. Combining field-theoretic arguments with numerical exact diagonalization and matrix-product-state methods, we find that the quantum critical point exhibits two-particle off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing. Our work shows that critical density fluctuations at a phase-separation instability can act as pairing glue for unconventional superconductivity in 1D, overcoming the disordering effect of phase fluctuations and the absence of long-lived fermionic quasiparticles in the normal state.

items.title: Topologically Obstructed Kondo Hybridization: A Route to Kondo Semimetals
items.summary: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles localized $f$ moments with conduction electrons, giving rise to coherent heavy-electron bands at low temperatures, typically characterized by a Kondo hybridization gap. Here we show, however, that the topology and symmetry of the conduction-electron Fermi surface can obstruct the opening of the Kondo hybridization gap at certain momenta. Treating the Fermi surface of a three-dimensional system as an effective two-dimensional manifold, we demonstrate that nontrivial topological invariants defined on this manifold impose a topological obstruction to opening a full hybridization gap, forcing the $fc$ hybridization to vanish at certain momenta on the Fermi surface. These hybridization zeros lead to crossings between $c$ and $f$ bands, giving rise to nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase. Our results establish topological obstructions to Kondo hybridization as a route to Kondo semimetals, revealing a fundamental connection between Fermi-surface topology and the emergence of correlated electronic phases.

items.title: High-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial
items.summary: We prove that, above a constant temperature threshold, Gibbs states of local noncommuting qudit Hamiltonians exhibit exponential decay of mutual information and conditional mutual information (CMI). Specifically, we prove exponential decay of the CMI for arbitrary spatial tripartitions $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ which need not comprise the entire system, thereby establishing a \textit{uniform Markov property} for high-temperature Gibbs states. A central obstruction to proving such bounds is that conventional cluster expansions for the logarithm of reduced Gibbs states can fail to converge due to noncommutativity. Our main insight is to construct a classical representation of the Gibbs state using an overcomplete basis. Although such representations generally involve negative quasiprobability weights, we show that a decomposition based on projective 2-designs admits a convergent cluster expansion with strictly positive weights at sufficiently high temperatures, allowing us to circumvent the obstruction. The separability of high-temperature Gibbs states is a natural byproduct of this decomposition. Finally, in the context of mixed-state phases of matter, our results imply that high-temperature Gibbs states belong to the same mixed-state phase as the maximally mixed state.

items.title: Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
items.summary: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.

items.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
items.summary: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

items.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
items.summary: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field. We illustrate the capabilities of this technique by applying it to two canonical problems. First, we directly observe the self-similar evolution of the velocity field in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows. Second, we map out the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, explicitly demonstrating the quantization of velocity circulation.

items.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
items.summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.

items.title: Local orbital magnetization and Chern markers from equilibrium local currents
items.summary: Local currents carry the orbital magnetization of a macroscopic sample and are key for modeling inhomogeneous magnetic materials and for understanding magnetoelectric and topological responses. However, producing realistic simulated images of local currents in inhomogeneous systems remains challenging. Building upon recent work on stochastic estimation methods for tight-binding models, we show that all matrix elements of positive semidefinite operators defined on a lattice can be obtained at once from a single set of filtered random vectors. This eliminates the need for independent simulations previously required for off-diagonal elements, which significantly speeds up the calculation of spatial maps of local currents. Further, we express bond currents in terms of loop currents that obey a discrete Poisson equation, with the current vorticity acting as the source term. Its solution yields a local orbital magnetization. In analogy with the global Středa relation, the derivative of this magnetization with respect to the chemical potential defines a new local Chern marker. Built entirely from bond currents, it requires no position operator and is not bound by the zero-sum rule of projector markers in open samples. Hence, it is free of boundary-compensation artifacts, and its sample average converges to the bulk Chern number in a controlled fashion.

items.title: Boundary-layer analysis of the partial engulfment of a small particle by a lipid membrane
items.summary: We study the axisymmetric partial engulfment of a small rigid sphere by a fluid Helfrich membrane. The neck that joins the wrapped cap to the membrane is an elastic boundary layer, which we analyse by matched asymptotic expansions. Its leading surface is a catenoid, which stores no bending energy and is obtained from the equilibrium equations for a regular inner expansion. Beyond the term linear in the size ratio, known from the literature, the energy contains a term proportional to the logarithm of the size ratio. Its coefficient is the effective lateral tension acting on the logarithmic excess area of the catenoid, and it depends on how the membrane is closed far from the particle. For a membrane in contact with a tension reservoir we obtain the wrapping energy to second order in the size ratio, in closed form at every wrapping angle. The resulting landscape contains as limits the low-tension regime and the local landscape of the wrapping problem previously derived in the literature, and describes the crossover between them. The landscape recovers the known binding threshold of a flat membrane, independent of tension and spontaneous curvature, and the bistability of the partially and fully wrapped states is controlled mainly by the spontaneous curvature. The order of the remainder is estimated, and the neck energy is checked against numerical solutions of the full nonlinear shape equations.

items.title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
items.summary: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear} when the {\em crossing of many-body energy levels} of bright and dark excitons occurs via phonon mediation. It also resembles the so-called field-like spin-transfer torque (STT) in spintronics, but STT is driven there with current pulses, so it explains the microscopic origin of the recently experimentally conjectured {\em excitonic STT}. Since dark excitons supply energy to magnons long after the fsLP is switched off, such a reservoir opens avenues for its engineering and applications in optospintronics and optomagnonics, neuromorphic computing, and quantum transduction.

items.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
items.summary: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

items.title: First-principles finite-size correction schemes for point defects of Cu$_3$N
items.summary: Point defects play a key role in determining semiconductor properties, such as electrical conductivity and photoluminescence, and often enable functional behavior. Accurate first-principles supercell simulations of point defects require reliable finite-size corrections. In this study, we combine PBE+U structural relaxations with HSE hybrid-functional calculations to determine defect formation energies and thermodynamic transition levels of Cu$_3$N. Finite-size trends are quantified using $Γ$-point calculations in supercells containing 256, 864, and 2048 atoms. We assess and extend the Makov-Payne and Lany-Zunger correction schemes by introducing additional $1/L^n$ terms, together with core-level potential alignment and defect-specific scaling models. Using Cu$_3$N as a case study, we show that charged vacancies are accurately described by the Makov-Payne-type scaling ($1/L + 1/L^{3}$), whereas interstitial defects with shallow or weakly localized electronic character are better captured by a hydrogenic impurity model that accounts for defect-band dispersion. Residual trends for neutral or weakly localized defects are described by higher-order polynomial fits in $1/L^{3}$ and $1/L^{4}$. Hybrid-functional energetics corrected using PBE+U-based finite-size trends confirm the intrinsic $p-n$ doping character of Cu$_3$N under the conditions considered and demonstrate that no single finite-size correction can be transferred across all defect types.

items.title: Activity-driven motion and deformation of a circular membrane domain
items.summary: Lipid bilayer membranes are nanometer-thin fluid interfaces characterized by both in-plane fluidity and lateral compositional heterogeneity. Cholesterol-rich liquid domains ("lipid rafts") are thought to regulate the spatial organization of membrane proteins and numerous cellular processes. While the passive diffusion and equilibrium shape fluctuations of membrane domains are well understood, much less is known about how the activity of molecular machines, such as protein pumps and enzymes, influences their mobility and deformation. Here, we analyze the dynamics of a membrane domain driven by an embedded molecular machine within the framework of two-dimensional Stokes flow. The molecular machine is modeled as a point singularity of the two-dimensional Stokes equations, including both rotational and irrotational singularities corresponding to force and source multipoles. We show that, despite being force-free, both force and source dipoles generate active flows that propel the membrane domain. For a force dipole undergoing rotational diffusion, the domain motion is diffusive at long times but exhibits a transient superdiffusive regime at intermediate times.

items.title: Reactivity-Informed Machine Learning for Performance Prediction and Design Space Exploration of Alkali-Activated Slag
items.summary: Establishing quantitative relationships among mix design, raw material properties, curing conditions, and performance remains a long-standing challenge in cementitious materials, particularly for alkali-activated materials with variable precursor and activator chemistry. Here, we curated the largest literature-derived alkali-activated slag (AAS) dataset to date, comprising over 3100 compressive strength records, 155 chemically distinct ground granulated blast-furnace slags (GGBSs), and 24 attributes incorporating precursor chemistry, fineness, and reactivity. Multiple machine learning (ML) algorithms were benchmarked across progressively enriched feature scenarios, demonstrating that integrating GGBS compositions, fineness, curing conditions, and specimen geometry improves predictive performance. The average metal oxide dissociation energy (AMODE), a physically interpretable representation of precursor reactivity, provides a compact alternative descriptor to explicit oxide compositions while enabling comparable predictive performance. Model interpretation revealed physically consistent trends from heterogeneous data, including non-monotonic effects of Na2O dosage and silicate modulus, reduced predicted strength at higher water content and larger specimen size, and coupled oxide-level effects more coherently represented by AMODE than by individual oxide contents. Statistically constrained design space exploration reveals reactivity-dependent trade-offs among strength, embodied CO2 emissions, and cost. The design maps identify high-strength regions with substantially lower CO2 emissions than OPC-based references at similar cost. Overall, this work demonstrates how reactivity-informed ML can extract physically meaningful trends from heterogeneous AAS data and guide source-dependent binder design. The curated dataset is publicly accessible to support advances in cement and concrete research.

items.title: Nematic equilibria on a Möbius strip: topology and extrinsic curvature
items.summary: We investigate the equilibrium configurations of a nematic liquid crystal confined in a thin tubular neighbourhood of a Möbius strip. Assuming degenerate tangential anchoring and a director uniform across the thickness, we derive an effective two-dimensional Frank energy that accounts for both the intrinsic and extrinsic curvature of the mid-surface. The non-orientability of the substrate imposes identification conditions that couple the reversal of the local frame to the head-to-tail symmetry of the nematic director. We show that the resulting topological classification depends on the parity of the number of half-twists: the sector index is a winding number for even parity, whereas only its parity is physically meaningful for odd parity, in which case the net director rotation is not quantised. We analyse the narrow-strip limit and solve the full two-dimensional equilibrium problem by finite-element methods. The competition between topological sectors depends on the strip aspect ratio and elastic anisotropy. In particular, for a single half-twist, the preferred sector changes at an aspect ratio of approximately 0.58, while for two half-twists two distinct minima of the same sector exchange their energy ordering near 0.60, without any change of topology. These results reveal how non-orientable topology and extrinsic curvature jointly shape nematic equilibria on curved substrates.

items.title: Optical Torque Reversal via Electric–Magnetic Spin-Channel Selection
authors: Lv Feng, 侣 冯, Ruohu Zhang, 若虎 张, Zhigang Li, 志刚 李, Bingjue Li, 冰珏 李, Dongdong Lin, 冬冬 林, Binfeng Yun, 斌峰 恽, Guanghao Rui and 光浩 芮
items.summary: Light carrying spin angular momentum (SAM) can exert optical torque and drive particles into rotational motion. Although optical torque reversal has been achieved by tailoring particle properties or incident field parameters, the respective roles of the electric and magnetic components of transverse SAM in governing the torque on an isotropic particle remain unresolved. Here, reversible control of the out-of- plane optical torque on an absorbing isotropic Mie sphere is demonstrated in interference fields formed by two or three plane waves. Two orthogonal linear polarization states selectively activate torque pathways mediated by the electric and magnetic components of the transverse SAM, while intermediate polarization states allow both pathways to coexist. Notably, polarization controls the optical torque by tuning the relative weights of electric and magnetic multipolar contributions. Once higher-order Mie channels become appreciable, competition among these contributions can reverse the total torque and switch the particle rotation between clockwise and counterclockwise directions. These results reveal distinct mechanical roles of the electric and magnetic components of transverse SAM and establish spin-channel selection as a mechanism for polarization-controlled optical torque reversal.

items.title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr6Sb6
authors: Hongye Zhang, Boqin Song, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Ying Zhu, Tianping Ying and Mingquan He
items.summary: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr6Sb6, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below TF ~ 70 K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of ~30–80 K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature Tp ~ 20–25 K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr6Sb6 as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

items.title: Following Photoexcited Structural Dynamics across Potential Energy Surfaces in Solids
Mineralogical evidence for hydrous carbonaceous chondrite relics in Chang’e-6 regolith
items.summary: Abstract Hydrous carbonaceous chondrites are potential carriers of exogenous water to the Earth–Moon system, yet well-preserved hydrous carbonaceous impactor fragments are rarely found in lunar samples, with previous discoveries limited to the lunar nearside. The Chang’e-6 mission returned the first sample from the farside, providing a unique opportunity to identify the exogenous materials that have added volatiles to this region. We document well‑preserved relics showing C1-like mineralogical features in a Chang’e-6 regolith breccia. They are dominated by fine-grained Mg-rich saponite with partially collapsed basal spacing, along with magnetite, dolomite, sulfides, and organic nanoglobules, matching mineral assemblages of heavily altered carbonaceous chondrites and hydrous materials returned from asteroids Ryugu and Bennu. This diagnostic mineral assemblage and in‑situ space‑weathering overprint confirm that these clasts are surviving fragments of the incoming impactor, and in situ dehydration records water loss during lunar surface exposure. Our study provides the first mineralogical and petrographic evidence for preserved hydrous carbonaceous impact debris in lunar farside regolith, revealing the microscale preservation of hydrated minerals and carbonaceous components and providing new constraints on impact-induced volatile injection and release from carbonaceous materials.

items.summary: The quasicrystals combined with nonreciprocal and on-site non-Hermiticity provide a unique platform to explore exceptional phenomena arising from the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). Especially, we investigate a non-Hermitian photonic lattice with nonreciprocal hoppings and staggered complex on-site potentials, revealing an energy-dependent bipolar NHSE and a quasiperiodicity-driven redistribution from skin states to bulk-localized states. Numerical winding numbers and analytical contact conditions reveal the spectral reconnections underlying the bipolar NHSE, with the sign of the imaginary eigenenergy determining its localization direction. Meanwhile, imaginary quasiperiodic modulation drives a crossover from skin localization to bulk localization, while real and imaginary modulations yield comparable bulk localization at strong modulation. Moreover, Fibonacci-size calculations support persistent skin–bulk coexistence, while a separable two-dimensional extension connects one-dimensional localization directions to corner accumulation and spatial redistribution. These results provide a unified framework for understanding and controlling the interplay between spectral topology and quasiperiodicity in non-Hermitian photonic systems.

items.title: Enhancing soil carbon to address the joint climate and biodiversity crises
High-rate and durable sodium-ion batteries enabled by charge-asymmetric single-atom-energized hard carbon
items.summary: Abstract Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) represent a promising complement to lithium-based systems due to the abundant supply and cost-effectiveness of sodium. However, the widespread adoption of SIBs is practically hindered by the lack of cycling-stable hard-carbon anodes with superior capacity and rate capability. Here, we show a design of high-rate and durable SIB anodes achieved by introducing main-group metal single atoms ( M SA = Sb, Bi, Sn) featuring a unique charge-asymmetric N 4 – M SA –O 2 moiety anchored on nitrogen-doped hard carbon ( M SA @NC). This designed charge-asymmetric configuration establishes a dynamically evolving atomic interface that adaptively modulates active sites to achieve significant improvements in both Na + storage kinetics and capacity. The representative Sb SA @NC system demonstrates high specific capacity, improved rate capability and cyclability in both coin and pouch-type cells. Extensive experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the structural rearrangement of the N 4 –Sb–O 2 moiety during (de)sodiation is highly reversible and energetically favorable, enabling enhanced reversible capacity (422.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 ) and rate capability (207.6 mAh g −1 at 20 A g −1 ) while preserving material integrity. This work offers a promising pathway in advancing high-performing HC anodes for fast-charging and durable SIBs.

items.title: Single-atom catalyst–Li2O2 interfacial chemistry governs the activity–stability trade-off in Li–O2 batteries
items.summary: Abstract Cathode catalysts in aprotic Li–O 2 batteries are commonly judged by their ability to lower charge overpotentials, yet improved catalytic activity often does not lead to durable cycling. Here, we use structurally well-defined M–N 4 single-atom catalysts (SACs) as model cathodes to elucidate the interplay between catalyst activity and battery stability. Integrated experimental and theoretical studies suggest that, although SACs promote Li 2 O 2 oxidation and lower the initial charging overpotential, they also increase the reactivity of discharge-generated Li 2 O 2 toward ether electrolytes, promoting carboxylate accumulation and cathode passivation. On the basis of this mechanistic insight, a localized high-concentration electrolyte is introduced to regulate the catalyst–Li 2 O 2 interfacial chemistry, suppress side reactions, and extend the cycling life from 42 to 398 cycles. This work identifies a previously overlooked trade-off between catalytic activity and battery stability in Li–O 2 batteries and provides a mechanistic foundation for designing stable catalyst/electrolyte interfaces in high-energy electrochemical devices.
